preamble.summary: Implements the whole of the provider-failures spec (§5.1 to §5.19, every §6 surface, every acceptance criterion). Each provider (Claude Code, Codex, Mistral Vibe) gets one pure session-outcome reader that turns an ended session into an answer or a failure. A failure carries a failure kind, the provider's own message and the session id when the provider reported one. The reader reads the provider's final result event first, then the transcript's last error event, then stderr, and never reads tool output or model text. Every adapter goes through these readers. The work runs in this order: an oracle pair freezes the reader's table of transcripts and kinds (phase-01, phase-02); the adapters raise typed session failures and write agent-error.log with the cause first (phase-03); every command prints the cause, the files and a retry hint, and a network failure exits 14 (phase-04); a run pauses on a network failure, a failed handoff turn is reported as itself, and fix-loop telemetry names its provider (phase-05); a stop's closing turn records a `network` close at review-stop 0.30.0 (phase-06); a failed decision record carries a required `failure` at 0.30.0 (phase-07); and an unknown visibility quotes gh, the cause prints before any secondary refusal (decide, authoring, run and resume), and the troubleshooting page lands (phase-08). Build on vibe-3 (#170): Vibe 3.0.3 writes an export.json on every exit, decoded by src/schemas/vibeExport.ts, whose outcome is reliable on 3.0.3. Only the outcome reading of the Vibe adapter changes. The decision-record-manifest `next` snapshot at 0.30.0 and its frozen 0.28.0 module already exist; review-stop moves from 0.26.0 to 0.30.0 here. Tests never read ~/.phax, a real ~/.claude, ~/.codex or ~/.vibe, the global git config or the real gh: they use tests/helpers/isolateGit.ts, temporary directories, makeFakeGitHub(), the fake backend, tests/helpers/fakeProviderCli.ts, and the fake `vibe` of tests/helpers/vibe3Fixtures.ts.
preamble.requiredCommandsNote: No new command. The configured `standard` gate verifies every phase. `pnpm exec tsx scripts/schemas-check.ts --write` (phases 06 and 07) is covered by the existing `pnpm exec tsx` allowance. Help text names exit codes in `src/cli/cliDocs.ts` (decide's `Exit codes:` line in both modes, review-code's failure exit, resume's refused-close exits), so phases 04 and 06 edit it and regenerate `phax.usage.kdl` and `docs/cli/reference.md` with `pnpm gen:usage-spec` and `pnpm docs:cli`, both allowed; `tests/integration/usageSpecDrift.test.ts` and `docsCliDrift.test.ts` keep them in step.
technicalArbitrations: Where the reader lives and what it returns: pure readers in src/domain/session/ (entry src/domain/session/outcome.ts, one module per provider), decoders in src/schemas/ (claudeOutput.ts, codexOutput.ts, vibeExport.ts), and the adapters in src/infra/providers/ spawn, read export.json and hand the lines, stderr, the end (exit code, signal or timeout) and the export read to the reader. It returns `SessionOutcome` = `{ kind: answer, provider, text, sessionId }` | `{ kind: failure, failure: { provider, kind, message, sessionId, resetAt } }`; the answer holds only `text`, so the Structured output spec can add a structured answer beside it. Loss accepted: no single place both reads and judges a session. The Vibe adapter still opens export.json itself, so an absent or unreadable export reaches the reader as a tagged input, not as the I/O error it was.

The error a failed session raises: a new tagged `AgentSessionFailedError` (carrying the `SessionFailure`, the agent-error.log path or null, the transcript path or null, and the paused phase id when a run sets one) for kinds network, provider-error, max-turns, killed and unknown. Limits keep `RateLimitError` / `UsageLimitError`, so RateLimitDetected, `rate_limited` and exit 8 stay as they are. They are built from the same failure, with `message` the failure line and `rawMessage` the provider message, and gain optional `agentErrorLog` and `transcript` paths, so a limit names its files too (§5.9). Loss accepted: two error families describe one outcome, so a caller that handles any failed session matches three tags, not one.

How a network failure is recognized: by the provider's verdict alone, matched against one shared table of connection signatures (ENOTFOUND, EAI_AGAIN, ECONNREFUSED, ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, `Can't reach the API server`, `Connection error`, `error sending request`, `stream disconnected`, `dns error`, `failed to lookup address`, `nodename nor servname`, `Network is unreachable`, `getaddrinfo`, ENETUNREACH, EHOSTUNREACH, `Request timed out`, `fetch failed`, `socket hang up`, and the httpx wordings Vibe passes through: `Name or service not known`, `Temporary failure in name resolution`, `All connection attempts failed`, `Connection refused`, `Server disconnected without sending a response`, `Timed out connecting to the model provider`, `Timed out waiting for the model to send its response`, `The model request timed out`). Claude Code: the `is_error` result event's `result` text (the synthetic `API Error: …`), else the last `system`/`api_retry` event's error, else stderr; the number of retries is not needed. Codex: the `turn.failed` error message, else the last `error` event, else stderr. Vibe: an export outcome other than `finished`, classified from the export's `error` (`{message, code}`) and outcome, else stderr. Vibe has no network code: a network failure arrives as code `backend_error` with httpx's message, which the table matches. Loss accepted: an outage worded outside the table reads as provider-error (exit 5, not resumable) until the table learns that wording.

How a run records a paused network failure: a new event `NetworkFailureDetected` beside `RateLimitDetected`, with the same dispositions and the same target states (run and phase `rate_limited`, the resume path a limit already proves). It persists `stoppedReason: network_failure` and `lastError` (the failure line), and writes resume instructions naming `phax resume <run>`. Loss accepted: run-status.json and `phax status` show the state `rate_limited` for an outage; only `stoppedReason` and `lastError` tell it from a limit. That is the price of the spec's non-goal: no failure kind and no new run state in run-status.json.

A failed handoff turn: a new event `HandoffTurnFailed` takes the transitions `HandoffMissing` takes, with `missing: []`, and also persists `lastError` (the failure line) and `stoppedReason: handoff_turn_failed`, so resume re-runs only the handoff. No HandoffMissing is dispatched for it. The pause re-raises an error carrying the session failure, so the CLI prints it and exits with its code. A limit in the handoff turn keeps its own path, and so does a spawn failure (`AgentInvocationError`). Loss accepted: the phase still reads `handoff_failed`, with no missing section, after a turn that failed rather than a handoff that was incomplete.

How the CLI orders the cause and a secondary refusal. The review commands write no record after a failed session, so they print only the cause lines. The use cases that do write one no longer print the record's warnings themselves: decide in both modes, headless authoring, and a run, whose phase that failed with a non-pausing kind writes its `failed` record (executePlan) and today prints `[phax] Warning: Phase "…" — records destination refused: …` straight to stderr before the CLI prints the cause. When there is one, they raise a `FailureWithFollowUpsError { cause, followUps }`; the CLI prints the cause's lines first and each follow-up after it. A follow-up reads `<kind> record refused, following the failed session: …` (`decision`, `authoring` or `phase`), and says so only when the cause is a session failure (an `AgentSessionFailedError` or a limit error); after any other cause (a refused answer, a spawn failure) the warning keeps today's wording. `exitCodeForError` and `exitCodeForAuthoringError` unwrap the cause. Loss accepted: the same failure reaches the CLI in two shapes, depending on whether the records step had anything to say.

Vibe refusals added by #170. Refusals before a session spawns are phax refusals, not session outcomes: the version floor, a user `accept-edits` profile, Vibe config under an extra root, and a missing transcript path. They keep their errors (`AgentInvocationError`, `SecurityEnforcementError`), their messages and today's agent-error.log (argv, then the message). A missing answer, a missing or invalid export, and an invalid export session id are `provider-error` failures carrying today's messages: the provider broke its own output contract. A config mismatch after the turn stays a phax refusal of a turn that ran (`AgentInvocationError`, exit 5, message kept), checked on failures too (next arbitration). Loss accepted: agent-error.log has two shapes; a refusal's log has no `failure:` header, so a reader tells a refusal from a failure by its first line.

Operator decision (2026-10-28, review finding): before honouring a failed Vibe turn, phax checks the effective config of every export that decodes and whose `config` is non-null, as it checks an answer's. A mismatch refuses the turn (`AgentInvocationError`, exit 5, not resumable, with today's message and agent-error.log) and takes precedence over the failure the reader returned. Loss accepted: a real outage that coincides with a config mismatch reads as the config refusal, not as a network failure (exit 5, not 14), so the person sees no retry hint for it. Kept because a secure turn that ran under a config phax did not set and then lost the network would otherwise pause with its edits kept, and a resume could commit them.

A failed decision record's `failure`. A session failure gives its kind; a refused answer (`DecideDocumentError`) gives `answer-refused`; the artifact changing during the session gives `artifact-changed`; a failed write or commit of the decided artifact gives `commit-failed`. Any other error after the writer started (a spawn failure, a Vibe refusal) gives `unknown`. The literals live in src/schemas/decisionRecord.ts, so the schemas package closure gains no domain module, and a type test keeps them equal to the reader's kinds plus the three. In memory, a failed record read from a stamp below 0.30.0 carries `failure: null`; the 0.30.0 file schema requires a value, so the writer cannot write null. Loss accepted: `unknown` also covers phax's own refusals, so the records branch cannot tell a refused spawn from a silent provider.

An interactive stop's first turn (interactive-session.json) lost to a network failure keeps its existing `provider-error` reason, with the failure line as its detail. No new reason is added: the spec adds failure kinds to no persisted shape other than the decision record and review-stop. Loss accepted: an outage at a first turn reads as a provider error in interactive-session.json.

run-list embeds the review-stop document as `stop`, so it moves to 0.30.0 with review-stop (a `next` snapshot and a frozen 0.26.0 module, a self-contained copy that inlines review-stop 0.26.0's shapes, since a frozen module imports only `effect`). Loss accepted: readers of `phax ls --json` learn a new stamp for a change that is only review-stop's.

The visibility port: `GitHub.visibility()` returns a reading `{ visibility, ghError }`, where `ghError` is gh's first non-empty stderr line (or the spawn error) when the query failed, else null. The network, auth or other class is a pure domain function, and the refusal's message and remedy are built in src/domain/records/destination.ts. Loss accepted: the init wizard and `configureRecords` adapt to the reading although they ignore its reason.

Codex: an agent turn with no answer message also fails (`provider-error`, no answer was found), not only a completion. Loss accepted: a Codex phase turn that did its work but ended without a final message, accepted today with empty text, now fails with exit 5.

Vibe outcomes come from Vibe 3.0.3's source, read at plan review on 2026-10-28. Outcomes and exits: `finished` 0; `usage_error`, `config_error` 1; `infrastructure_failure` 2 (the model API after its retries, or the runtime); `turn_limit`, `token_limit`, `price_limit`, `deadline`, `terminated`, `length`, `refusal` 3; `aborted` 4. The export's `error` is `{message (required), code: string | null}`; the codes are `rate_limit`, `context_too_long`, `response_too_long`, `refusal`, `invalid_image_attachment`, `images_not_supported`, `compaction_failed`, `incomplete_stream`, `backend_error`, `invalid_model`, `invalid_api_key`, `internal_error`. Mapping: `turn_limit` → max-turns; `terminated` and `deadline` → killed (Vibe catches SIGTERM, writes `terminated` and exits 3, so a phax timeout kill reads from the export, not from a signal); code `rate_limit` → rate-limit; `invalid_api_key` → provider-error; any other failure is classified from its message by the shared tables (a network failure is `backend_error` with httpx's text), else provider-error. `session_id`, `usage`, `cost_usd`, `steps` and `config` are all nullable in a failure export, so the outcome read decodes them as nullable while `extractVibeExportUsage` keeps its meaning (a null usage or cost gives no usage). Loss accepted: how the `vibe-rs` binary maps a turn error to the export's outcome was read from its strings, not its source; a wording outside the tables reads as provider-error until they learn it.

Reading a session's end needs its signal. spawnClaude, spawnCodex and spawnVibe report the signal or timeout that ended the process, alongside the exit code. In the Vibe adapter this counts as reading its session outcome. Loss accepted: none beyond a touch of the Vibe spawn's close handler.

The provider's verdict decides over the exit code: a Claude `is_error: false` result with text, a Codex `turn.completed` with an answer message, or a Vibe `finished` export, followed by a non-zero exit, now reads as an answer. Loss accepted: a provider that reports success and then crashes on its way out is trusted; today such a session fails with `exited with code N`.

`phax plans overlap` extracts with the LLM fallback and wraps every error into `AnalyzePlanOverlapError`, so a network failure there exits as today, never 14. Loss accepted: that one command gives no retry hint for an outage; the plan leaves its error wrapping alone.

phases.title: Session outcome contract and its oracles
phases.objective: Fix the contract every provider's session is read through: the session outcome, the failure kinds and the three reader entries. Freeze the table of transcripts and the outcome each must read as, as oracles the next phase discharges.
detailedInstructions: Create `src/domain/session/outcome.ts`, pure: no I/O and no `node:` import. Its only import is the `ProviderId` type from `src/domain/routing/types.ts`. Export exactly: `FailureKind` = `network` | `rate-limit` | `usage-limit` | `provider-error` | `max-turns` | `killed` | `unknown`; `FAILURE_KINDS`, those literals in that order; `SessionFailure` { provider: ProviderId; kind: FailureKind; message: string; sessionId: string | null; resetAt: string | null }; `SessionOutcome` = { kind: `answer`; provider; text: string; sessionId: string | null } | { kind: `failure`; failure: SessionFailure }; `SessionEnd` = { kind: `exited`; code: number } | { kind: `signalled`; signal: string } | { kind: `timed-out` }; `EndedSession` { lines: readonly string[] (stdout, one JSON line each); stderr: string; end: SessionEnd }; `VibeExportRead` = { kind: `not-requested` } | { kind: `absent`; path } | { kind: `unreadable`; path; detail } | { kind: `text`; path; text }.

In the same file, export the functions `isTransientFailure(kind: FailureKind): boolean`, `readClaudeOutcome(ended: EndedSession): SessionOutcome`, `readCodexOutcome(ended: EndedSession): SessionOutcome` and `readVibeOutcome(ended: EndedSession, exported: VibeExportRead): SessionOutcome`. Each body throws `new Error("not implemented: <function name>")`, with its parameters prefixed `_` for the linter. These stubs are what the oracles compile and load against.

Document the contract in a module comment, which the next phase implements. Reading order: (1) the provider's final result event decides: a Claude `result` event, a Codex `turn.failed` or `turn.completed`, or a Vibe export with an outcome; (2) with none, a process that ended on a signal or a timeout is `killed`; (3) otherwise the transcript's last error event (a Claude `system`/`api_retry` error, a Codex `error` event); (4) otherwise stderr's first non-empty lines, at most three, joined by a space; (5) otherwise `unknown`, with no session id unless an init or thread event gave one. Tool output (Claude `user` tool_result content, Codex `command_execution` output) and model text (assistant messages) are never read to classify or to word a failure. The provider message is the deciding source's own text. The kind is read from that text: usage-limit signatures before rate-limit, then network signatures; otherwise `provider-error`, or `max-turns` for a turn-limit verdict. The session id comes from the result event, else from the Claude `system`/`init` event, the Codex `thread.started` event or the Vibe export.

Create `tests/unit/session/outcome.test.ts`. Every test carries the `it.fails` marker, has a distinct title and imports only from `src/domain/session/outcome.ts`. It imports every exported type and function of that module (types with `import type`), so knip, which has no entry under src/domain/session/, sees each export used. Its fixtures are written by hand in the file, as objects passed to `JSON.stringify`, with no generator and no helper module outside the file. Session ids are valid UUIDs. Assert with `toEqual` on the kind, provider, session id and resetAt, and with `toBe` or `toContain` on messages, exactly as each case below states.

Claude Code cases: (a) init, assistant text, a result with subtype `success`, `is_error: false`, `result: PONG`, exit 0 → answer `PONG` with the result's session id; (b) init, then a result with subtype `error_during_execution`, `is_error: true`, no `result` key and a session id, exit 1 → `provider-error`, message contains `error_during_execution`, session id the result's; (c) a result with subtype `error_max_turns`, `is_error: true`, no `result`, exit 1 → `max-turns` with that session id; (d) the DNS outage: init, ten `{type: system, subtype: api_retry, attempt, max_retries: 10, retry_delay_ms, error_status: null, error: Connection error., session_id}` events, a synthetic assistant message (model `<synthetic>`) holding the API Error text, then a result with `is_error: true` and `result: API Error: Can't reach the API server — check your internet or DNS (ENOTFOUND)`, exit 1 → `network`, message exactly that text, session id the result's; (e) a `user` tool_result whose content is `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`, an assistant text saying `I hit a rate limit`, then the `error_during_execution` result, exit 1 → `provider-error`, not a limit; (f) a result with `is_error: true` and `result: Claude AI usage limit reached|1793120400`, stderr `Error: something else broke`, exit 1 → `usage-limit`, message the result's text, resetAt `new Date(1793120400 * 1000).toISOString()`; (g) a result with `is_error: true` and `result: API Error: 429 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"rate_limit_error"}}` → `rate-limit`; (h) no line, empty stderr, end signalled `SIGTERM` → `killed`, message contains `SIGTERM`, session id null; (i) no line, empty stderr, exit 1 → `unknown`, session id null; (j) init only, stderr `Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:443`, exit 1 → `network` from stderr, session id the init's; (k) a result with `is_error: true` and `result: API Error: 500 Internal server error`, exit 0 → `provider-error` (an error result is a failure whatever the exit code).

Codex cases: (l) `thread.started`, an `item.completed` agent_message `DONE`, `turn.completed`, exit 0 → answer `DONE` with the thread id; (m) `thread.started`, then `turn.failed` with `error.message: stream disconnected before completion: error sending request for url (https://api.openai.com/v1/responses)`, exit 1 → `network`, message exactly that; (n) an `error` event with `message: You've hit your usage limit. Try again later.`, exit 1 → `usage-limit`; (o) `thread.started`, `turn.completed`, no agent_message, exit 0 → `provider-error`, message contains `no answer`; (p) `turn.failed` with `error.message: unexpected status 400 Bad Request: model not supported` → `provider-error`, message exactly that; (q) an `item.completed` command_execution whose `aggregated_output` is `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`, then `turn.failed` with `error.message: tool crashed` → `provider-error`, not a limit.

Vibe cases, the export written as Vibe 3.0.3 writes it (`error` is null or `{message, code}` with `message` required and `code` a string or null), stream entries as tests/helpers/vibe3Fixtures.ts shows them, written by hand here: (r) export `{schema_version: 1, session_id, usage, cost_usd, outcome: finished, exit_code: 0, error: null, vibe_version: 3.0.3}` and a stream whose last assistant message has text `PONG`, exit 0 → answer `PONG` with the export's session id; (s) export outcome `config_error`, exit_code 1, `session_id: null`, `error: {message: Invalid API key (from env var MISTRAL_API_KEY), code: invalid_api_key}`, exit 1 → `provider-error`, message contains `Invalid API key` and `invalid_api_key`, session id null; (t) export outcome `infrastructure_failure`, exit 2, `error: {message: API error occurred: Status 400. reasoning_effort low is not supported for this model, code: backend_error}` → `provider-error`, message contains `reasoning_effort low is not supported`; (u) export outcome `infrastructure_failure`, exit 2, `error: {message: [Errno 8] nodename nor servname provided, or not known, code: backend_error}` → `network`, message contains `nodename nor servname`; (u2) export outcome `infrastructure_failure`, `error: {message: Too many requests, code: rate_limit}` → `rate-limit`; (u3) export outcome `turn_limit`, exit 3, `error: null` → `max-turns` with the export's session id; (u4) export outcome `terminated`, exit 3, `error: null` → `killed`, and the same for outcome `deadline`; (u5) a failure export whose `session_id`, `usage`, `cost_usd`, `steps` and `config` are all null, outcome `infrastructure_failure`, `error: {message: All connection attempts failed, code: backend_error}` → `network`, session id null (the export still decodes); (v) `not-requested` (a completion), stderr `Error: 429 rate limited`, exit 1 → `rate-limit`; (w) `absent` export at a path, exit 0 → `provider-error`, message contains that path.
Add one table test that `isTransientFailure` is true exactly for `network`, `rate-limit` and `usage-limit` over `FAILURE_KINDS`.
Run the configured gate: every oracle passes while it is marked, because its stub throws.
phases.boundaryContracts: Producer: src/domain/session/outcome.ts (domain). The stable shape is `SessionOutcome` and `SessionFailure`. The reader does no I/O; the adapter owns spawning and reading files.

commit.subject: test(session): oracles for the session outcome readers
commit.body: Fix the session outcome contract (failure kinds, SessionFailure, SessionOutcome, the ended-session input and the three reader entries) in src/domain/session/outcome.ts, with stub readers that throw. Freeze the table of provider transcripts and the outcome each must read as, as expected-failure oracles: Claude Code error results, the DNS outage, limits read only from the provider's verdict, killed and silent sessions, Codex failures, Vibe's export outcomes and error codes as Vibe 3.0.3 writes them, and the empty Codex answer.

phases.assignmentReason: The phase designs the session outcome contract and its fixture table across three providers, a shape no code in the repository holds yet.

phases.title: Session outcome readers
phases.objective: Implement the three readers behind the contract, so every provider session reads into exactly one outcome by the provider's own verdict, and discharge the oracles.
detailedInstructions: Remove every `it.fails` marker from `tests/unit/session/outcome.test.ts`, turning each into `it`. Change nothing else in that file: removing the markers is this phase's only change to it.

Decoders in src/schemas. In `src/schemas/claudeOutput.ts`, add decoders for a Claude stream result event whose `result` is optional, with `subtype`, `is_error`, `session_id` and an optional `errors` string array; for the `system`/`init` event (its `session_id`); and for the `system`/`api_retry` event (an `error` that is a string or an object with a string `message`). Unknown keys are dropped. Reuse what `src/schemas/claudeStream.ts` already decodes where it fits. Keep the existing exports (`findResultEvent`, `hasErroredResultEvent`, `classifyRateLimit`, `normalizeResetAt`): the adapters still use them until phase-03 removes them. In `src/schemas/codexOutput.ts`, add decoders for `turn.completed`, `turn.failed` (`error.message`) and `error` (`message`) events. In `src/schemas/vibeExport.ts`, add a decoder for outcome reading that takes the export as Vibe 3.0.3 writes it: `error` is null or `{message: string, code: string | null}`, and `session_id`, `usage`, `cost_usd`, `steps` and `config` may each be null. Leave `readVibeExport` and `extractVibeExportUsage` with their meaning (a null usage or cost still gives no usage). Every export that decodes today must still decode.

Create `src/domain/session/signatures.ts`: the shared, case-insensitive network signature table listed in the plan's Technical arbitrations; the usage-limit signatures (usage limit, monthly limit, quota exceeded or reached), checked before the rate-limit ones (rate limit, rate-limited, too many requests, a standalone 429, rate_limit_error); and the reset-time extraction. Copy the reset patterns and the epoch and ISO normalization from `src/schemas/claudeOutput.ts`, so resetAt is an ISO instant or null. One `classifyVerdictText(text)` returns `network`, `rate-limit`, `usage-limit` or null. It is only ever applied to a provider verdict.

Create `src/domain/session/claudeOutcome.ts`. The last decodable result event decides. `is_error: false` with a `result` string is an answer. `is_error: true` with result text is classified by that text; with no match it is `provider-error` with that text, or `max-turns` when its subtype is `error_max_turns`. `is_error: true` without result text is `max-turns` for `error_max_turns`, else `provider-error` whose message is the subtype, followed by `: ` and the first `errors` entry when there is one. An error result fails whatever the exit code. With no result event, apply the reading order of the module comment in outcome.ts (killed, last api_retry error, stderr, unknown), and take the session id from the init event.

Create `src/domain/session/codexOutcome.ts`. The session id comes from `thread.started`. A `turn.failed` decides (its message classified, else `provider-error`). commit.subject: feat(session): read each provider's session outcome
commit.body: Implement the Claude Code, Codex and Mistral Vibe session readers behind src/domain/session/outcome.ts. Each turns an ended session into an answer, or a failure with its kind, the provider's own message and the session id it reported. The reading order is the final result event, then the signal or timeout, then the last error event, then stderr; tool output and model text are never read. Network and limit verdicts share one signature table. New decoders cover Claude error results with no result text, api_retry and init events, Codex turn and error events, and the Vibe export's error. commit.subject: feat(providers): fail sessions through the outcome readers
commit.body: The Claude Code, Codex and Mistral Vibe adapters now read every ended session through its outcome reader. A failure raises AgentSessionFailedError (or a limit error for the limit kinds) carrying the failure kind, the provider's message, the session id and the paths of agent-error.log and the transcript. agent-error.log opens with the failure, provider, message, session and transcript lines. phases.title: Unknown visibility says why, and the cause comes first
phases.objective: An unknown repository visibility quotes gh's first stderr line and suggests a retry for a network or auth failure. A record refusal after a failed session prints after the failure and says it follows it. The troubleshooting page explains a failed agent session.
detailedInstructions: Create `src/domain/records/ghFailure.ts`: `classifyGhFailure(firstLine: string | null)` returns `network` (error connecting to, could not resolve host, dial tcp, no such host, connection refused, i/o timeout, TLS handshake timeout; never a bare `could not resolve`, which gh's `GraphQL: Could not resolve to a Repository` not-found error also says, nor a bare `timeout`), `auth` (gh auth login, authentication, not logged in, HTTP 401, Bad credentials) or `other`. Pure and case-insensitive.

`src/domain/records/destination.ts`: the destination check takes a visibility reading `{ visibility, ghError }`. An unknown visibility's refusal reads `this repo's visibility could not be determined — gh: <first line>` (the plain message when `ghError` is null). Its remedy is `retry once the network is back` for network, `run \`gh auth login\`, then retry` for auth, and today's `acknowledgedUnknownVisibility` remedy for other or no line. A refusal for network or auth never mentions acknowledgedUnknownVisibility. What the destination accepts is unchanged: an unknown visibility is still refused.

`src/ports/github.ts`: `visibility(repo)` returns that reading. `src/infra/github.ts`: a failed `gh repo view` keeps gh's first non-empty stderr line (or the spawn error's message when gh could not run) as `ghError`. `src/infra/fakes/github.ts`: keep `setVisibility`, and add `failVisibility(firstLine)`. Adapt `src/app/recordPlumbing.ts`, `src/app/initWizard.ts` and `src/app/configureRecords.ts` to the reading.

Cause before secondary refusals. In `src/domain/errors.ts`, add `FailureWithFollowUpsError { message, cause, followUps: readonly string[] }`. In `src/app/decideVerdicts.ts`, `src/app/decideArtifact.ts` and `src/app/authorArtifact.ts`, the failure path still writes the record, but no longer prints the record's refusal and push warnings to `input.output`. When there is at least one, it fails with `FailureWithFollowUpsError` around the original error, otherwise with the original error. Record warnings after a failed session read `decision record refused, following the failed session: …` (and `authoring record …`): give `decisionRecordWarning` in `src/app/writeDecisionRecord.ts` and `recordWarning` in authorArtifact a flag for it, set only when the cause is a session failure (an `AgentSessionFailedError` or a limit error); after any other cause, such as a refused answer, the warning keeps today's wording. `exitCodeForError` and `exitCodeForAuthoringError` in `src/cli/commands/runLayers.ts` return the cause's code. `src/cli/commands/artifactDecide.ts` and `src/cli/commands/artifact.ts` print the cause's lines first (renderSessionFailure, or the existing rendering for other errors), then each follow-up as a warning.

Runs. A phase that fails with a non-pausing kind writes its `failed` record in `src/app/executePlan.ts` (`failOnRefusal: false`), and `writeRecordForPhase` prints `[phax] Warning: Phase "…" — records destination refused: …` straight to stderr before the CLI prints the cause. For a phase whose session failed, collect that warning (and any push warning) instead, worded `phase record refused, following the failed session: …`, and fail with `FailureWithFollowUpsError` around the session failure. `src/cli/commands/run.ts` and `src/cli/commands/resume.ts` print the cause's lines first, then each follow-up as a warning, and exit with the cause's code. A record refusal after a phase that did not fail on its session keeps printing as today.

Docs. Create `docs/agent-session-failures.md`, `Troubleshooting a failed agent session`, for an operator whose command just failed on an agent session and who wants to know whether to retry, resume or fix something. Walk through the DNS outage case: the `claude-code session failed (network)` line, the agent-error.log it names, the record refusal that follows it, and the retry or `phax resume` it suggests. Then list the exit codes 5, 8 and 14 and what to do for each. Register it in `site/pages.ts` beside the upgrading guide. In `README.md` § Troubleshooting, add a bullet for a failed agent session and for exit 14 linking the page, and make the unknown-visibility advice match the new remedies.

Tests. Create `tests/integration/githubVisibility.test.ts`, a contract suite run against NodeGitHubLayer, with a fake `gh` on PATH as tests/integration/githubRepoWebUrl.test.ts does, and against makeFakeGitHub(): success, a network failure, an auth failure and a no-GitHub-remote failure. Extend `tests/unit/recordsDestination.test.ts` for the three remedies, with the three gh lines of the spec's surface. Create `tests/integration/decideFailureOrder.test.ts`: `runArtifactDecide` in verdicts mode with a fake backend failing the writer, transcripts on and an in-repo destination, and a fake GitHub whose visibility fails with `error connecting to api.github.com`. The session failure line comes before `decision record refused, following the failed session`, the refusal quotes `gh: error connecting to api.github.com`, and the exit code is 14. Create `tests/integration/runFailureOrder.test.ts`: a run whose phase session fails with kind provider-error (fake backend), records on with transcripts and an in-repo destination, and a fake GitHub whose visibility fails, prints the failure line before `phase record refused, following the failed session`, and exits 5.
